title: Geometrically reduced fibres near a geometrically reduced generic fibre
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Suppose $Y$ is irreducible [def-weil-irreducible-components] with generic point $\eta$ [def-sc-generic-point], and suppose the generic fibre $X_\eta$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is geometrically reduced over $\kappa(\eta)$ [def-weil-residue-field, def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Then there exists a nonempty open subset $V\subseteq Y$ such that for every $y\in V$, the fibre $X_y$ is geometrically reduced over $\kappa(y)$. No flatness, reducedness of $Y$, Noetherianity, or nonemptiness of the fibres is assumed.

proof.text: Base change to the reduction $r:Y_{\mathrm{red}}\to Y$. The cited reduction result makes $r$ a homeomorphism and $Y_{\mathrm{red}}$ reduced. It is irreducible because its underlying space is that of $Y$, hence integral by the stated characterization of integrality. Residue fields are unchanged: locally the quotient $R\to R/\sqrt{0}$ induces $(R/\sqrt{0})_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak p=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. Associativity of the fibre product therefore identifies the old and new fibres over every point, including $\eta$. Finite type is preserved by the cited base-change theorem. Any nonempty good open of $Y_{\mathrm{red}}$ corresponds to a nonempty open of $Y$ with exactly the same fibres. It is therefore enough to prove the assertion with $Y$ integral. Restrict further to a nonempty affine open of $Y$; it contains $\eta$, and an open found there is also open in the original base.

Apply generic flatness and local finite presentation to $f$ over the integral base. This gives a nonempty open $W\subseteq Y$ on which $f$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. Replace $Y$ by $W$ and $X$ by $X_W$. The generic point remains in $W$, its fibre is unchanged, and finite type persists by base change. These replacements suffice because any nonempty open obtained in $W$ is nonempty open in $Y$. The generic fibre is locally finitely presented: on each affine presentation $A\to A[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(h_1,\ldots,h_m)$, tensoring with $\kappa(\eta)$ gives $\kappa(\eta)[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(\bar h_1,\ldots,\bar h_m)$. The affine fibre-product formula identifies these algebras with the fibre charts.

source.place: Tag 0578, first paragraph, using morphisms.tex Tag 052A, proposition-generic-flatness

proof.text: Record a finiteness fact for every fibre $X_y$, including $X_\eta$. By finite-type base change it is of finite type over the field $\kappa(y)$, so it has a finite affine cover $\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ with each $B_i$ a finite type $\kappa(y)$-algebra. A field is Noetherian, since its only ideals are $0$ and the whole field. The finite-type algebra theorem and the affine-space theorem cited here show that each $\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ is topologically Noetherian. A descending chain of closed subsets of $X_y$ stabilizes after restriction to each of these finitely many affine charts; taking the maximum of the stabilization indices shows that it stabilizes on $X_y$. Thus $X_y$ is topologically Noetherian. Every subset of it is quasi-compact by the cited compactness theorem. In particular every open immersion into $X_y$ is quasi-compact: its inverse image of an affine open is such a subset. It is also quasi-separated, since the diagonal of an open immersion is an isomorphism. These facts will justify both density lemmas below without any quasi-separatedness hypothesis on $f$.

source.place: Tag 0578, density argument with its implicit quasi-compactness hypotheses made explicit; algebra.tex Tag 00FN; topology.tex Tag 04ZA

proof.text: Let $U\subseteq X$ be the union of the open subschemes on which $f$ is smooth. Apply the dense-smooth-locus theorem to the locally finitely presented geometrically reduced $\kappa(\eta)$-scheme $X_\eta$. Its smooth locus is dense. At each point of that locus, the pointwise fibre criterion applies to $f$, because $f$ is flat and locally of finite presentation after step 2. It gives a smooth neighbourhood in $X$. Hence this dense locus lies in $U_\eta$, so $U_\eta$ is dense in $X_\eta$. Also, every $U_y$ is geometrically reduced: it is covered by the fibres of the smooth opens defining $U$; those fibres are geometrically reduced by the smooth-fibre theorem. After any field extension their corresponding opens still cover, and reducedness on an open cover implies reducedness of the whole base-changed $U_y$. This last deduction uses only the cited open-cover criterion.

source.place: Tag 0578, second paragraph; varieties.tex Tag 056V and morphisms.tex Tags 01V9, 02V4

proof.text: The identity field extension in geometric reducedness shows that $X_\eta$ is reduced. The inclusion $U_\eta\hookrightarrow X_\eta$ has dense topological image by step 4, and is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by step 3. The reduced-target dense-image theorem therefore says that its scheme-theoretic image is all of $X_\eta$. By the kernel description of that image, the sheaf map $\mathcal O_{X_\eta}\to (j_\eta)_*\mathcal O_{U_\eta}$ is injective. Thus $U_\eta$ is scheme-theoretically dense in the sense required by the next step.

source.place: Tag 0578, second paragraph, invoking morphisms.tex Tag 056D, lemma-reduced-scheme-theoretically-dense

proof.text: Apply the schematic-density spreading lemma to the finite type morphism $f:X\to Y$ and the open $U$ just constructed. Its base is irreducible with generic point $\eta$, and its generic-fibre injectivity hypothesis was proved in step 5. It supplies a nonempty open $V\subseteq Y$ such that $U_y$ is scheme-theoretically dense in $X_y$ for all $y\in V$.

Fix $y\in V$ and a field extension $L/\kappa(y)$. To verify density after this extension, work on an arbitrary affine open $C=\operatorname{Spec}D\subseteq X_y$. The restriction $U_y\cap C\to C$ is schematically dense by restriction of the injective sheaf map in step 6. It is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by step 3. The affine fibre-product formula identifies $C_L$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(D\otimes_{\kappa(y)}L)$. The field-extension theorem makes $D\to D\otimes_{\kappa(y)}L$ faithfully flat, hence flat; the flat affine criterion then makes $C_L\to C$ flat. Apply flat pullback of dense images to obtain that $(U_y\cap C)_L\to C_L$ has scheme-theoretic image $C_L$. By the image-kernel description, this means that its structure-sheaf map is injective. Its source is an open of $(U_y)_L$, which is reduced by step 4.

source.place: Tag 081I, lemma-flat-base-change-scheme-theoretic-image; geometric refinement of the Tag 0578 use of Tag 056E

proof.text: For any open $T\subseteq C_L$, a nilpotent section of $\mathcal O_{C_L}(T)$ maps to a nilpotent section on $T\cap (U_y\cap C)_L$. That section is zero because the open source is reduced. Injectivity from step 7 forces the original section to be zero. Hence $C_L$ is reduced by the section-wise definition. The affine opens $C$ cover $X_y$, so their pullbacks $C_L$ cover $(X_y)_L$, and the open-cover criterion proves that $(X_y)_L$ is reduced. Since $L/\kappa(y)$ was arbitrary, $X_y$ is geometrically reduced. This holds for every $y\in V$. The reductions in steps 1 and 2 transfer this same nonempty good open back to the original base. Empty fibres cause no exception: their sections have no nonzero nilpotents and all the covering/injectivity arguments are vacuous.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q51-eeebf5bef (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery and the sources: Stacks 0578 (more-morphisms 7215-7255), 0573 (6563-6641), and morphisms 01RE, 056D, 056E and 081I. The item statement is unchanged and matches 0578. Step-by-step check. Step 1: going to Y_red keeps the residue fields and the fibres; the calculation is written out. Step 2: generic flatness gives only flatness and local finite presentation, and only that is used. It is a declared off-unit tool use, which I accept. Step 3: every fibre is topologically Noetherian, so the inclusions of opens are quasi-compact and quasi-separated, which the Nagata lemmas need. Step 4: a dense smooth locus plus the pointwise fibre criterion makes U_eta dense; smooth opens give geometrically reduced U_y through the open-cover node. Step 5: 056D gives that U_eta is scheme-theoretically dense, i.e. the sheaf map is injective. Step 6: the new child applies with exactly its hypotheses. Steps 7-8: on affine charts, flat pullback (081I) through the faithfully flat D->D⊗L, then the section-wise 056E argument, give reducedness after every field extension. This correctly fills in what the source's bare 056E step leaves out. New node lem-trf-schematic-density-generic-fibre-open: it is Stacks 0573 with density written as sheaf injectivity (01RE). It is true; tested on Z[x]/(px) with U=D(p), on an empty generic fibre and on U=X. It has no proof sketch, cites its definitions, and records searches of all three kinds. It is not a clause of the item, and grep finds no existing 0573 node. The 0559, 0577 and preparation nodes are different statements. No SGA anywhere. Advisory: under the blueprint_update of def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image, step 7 also needs (U_y∩C)_L->C_L quasi-compact; it is, because C_L is Noetherian. No fixes.
